newsitem.title: USA: Claridge notes up on talks with Hilton.
newsitem.headline: Claridge notes up on talks with Hilton.

text.p: Claridge Hotel and Casino's 11-3/4 percent first mortgage notes posted a dramatic rise on Friday after the company said it is in acquisition talks with Hilton Hotels Corp, traders said.

The notes were last seen trading at 77-3/4, up nine and a half points from Thursday's close. The issue was quoted at 77-5/8 bid, 78-3/8 offer, traders said, adding that more than $3 million had traded.
The issue had been mired in the 60s since the company said in November it was unlikely it would be able to make its February 1 interest payment.
Prices rose as Hilton, which already owns 35 percent to 40 percent of the notes, said its offer would include a buyback of the remainder at a 10 percent premium, traders and analysts said.
Under a prepackaged bankruptcy plan, Hilton would acquire all Claridge stock in exchange for its funding the cash distribution to noteholders.
Claridge said it will default on the interest payment.
Matthew Ferko, high-yield analyst at BT Securities Corp, said a Hilton takeover is a excellent deal for bondholders, who would otherwise have a difficult time urging prices higher than the 60s.
"Based on the financial results of the Claridge, you'd have to make some generous assumptions about improvements in their cash flow to warrant a trading price in the mid-70s," Ferko said.
Claridge's adjusted 12-month cash flow would have had to grow to $15 million from the $4.8 million reported as of September 30 for the bonds to be valued at 76, Ferko said.
The analyst said Claridge's 502 room base and parking garage were primary targets for Hilton's neighboring property.
